residuals.what: Plateau where no heavier setting allows the target repetitions with the reserve (machine steps that are coarse relative to the load), most visible in LOAD mode, where a STRENGTH-goal machine MAIN holds R at a fixed target.
residuals.whyAcceptable: Not harmful: the dose holds and is offered the step again at the existing cadence. Holding a dose still yields benefit; continued progress needs overload (CL-5). Disclosed, non-blocking for a shadow reference; adding LOAD-mode repetition progression would be a new dose rule.

residuals.what: The engine cannot verify that H is exactly one setting above R; an athlete who jumps two settings and meets ADVANCE with verification is adopted at H.
residuals.whyAcceptable: Adoption still needs the target repetitions at the prescribed reserve (executed capacity) and a confirmed or repeated value; the at-or-below-plan rule and the KNOWN-row 'otherwise reduce it' instruction correct an overshoot at the next exposure.

residuals.what: Reserve (RIR) self-report is imprecise (about one repetition, heterogeneous); the appropriateness of a coarse step rests on it.
residuals.whyAcceptable: Existing R6 limitation (RIR treated as approximate; the ADVANCE gate already tolerates one repetition); unchanged by this rule (CL-6).

residuals.what: Machine identity is not modelled: the same exercise on another machine or gym yields non-comparable values that can be verified and adopted.
residuals.whyAcceptable: Existing equipment-detail gap (B0-F07, Product/Data). A lighter value is adopted as executed evidence and a heavier one needs ADVANCE and verification, so the reference follows what is lifted.

residuals.what: Numeric plausibility of logged values (typos inside 0-500 kg).
residuals.whyAcceptable: Existing open Data gap (SSCTR R5, D45); the same-value agreement or confirmation catches a single typo before adoption.

residuals.what: Self-selected loads tend to be light; the athlete may choose a setting below the instruction's intent.
Each step costs one load question when the exercise appears once a week and the athlete does not confirm in the review.

recheckObservations.title: F03-B: a valid second equal log can be missed when the week of the first log is reviewed KEEP and is not complete
recheckObservations.reproduction: probes/f03b-verify-gap.mjs CoachingCore HYPERTROPHY PIN 4 9: leg press logged 150 on the next-setting rows of weeks 2, 4, 5 and 6; one accessory (leg-curl-machine) logged in an unknown unit in week 4, whose review is KEEP. Questions at weeks 2, 4 and 5; adoption only from week 6's log (plan states 150 from week 7). CLEAN control (same athlete, no unknown unit): the week-5 log verifies.
recheckObservations.mechanism: The evidence reducer re-reads a week that no non-KEEP review closed and that is not complete through strengthAtBreak (facts only), which by its documented contract adopts nothing and ignores non-KNOWN rows, so the machine pending setting from that week is lost. Pre-existing reducer mechanism (the D45 establishment pendingLoad has the same exposure); F03-B depends on it.
recheckObservations.domainEffect: Conservative: adoption delayed, one or two extra questions; no undue dose; the athlete keeps training at the setting the row allows. Rule residual R-07 ('at most one question per step') does not hold in this shape.
routing: Engineering (later mission; the engineering check may confirm)

recheckObservations.title: F03-B: a log at R on a next-setting row is gated against the step's repetitions, not the fallback's
recheckObservations.reproduction: probes/f03b-cadence-hold.mjs CoachingCore SHORT: leg press next-setting row (8 reps at the next setting, fallback 140 kg x 12) logged at 140 kg x 9 -> gate ADVANCE; the fallback dose 140 x 12 is held and the step re-offered. The dumbbell control logged 3 reps short -> REGRESS.
recheckObservations.domainEffect: Doses stay within executed capacity (140 x 12 was executed before). But an underperformance at R on a step row is not counted toward the repeated-missed-reps REGRESS, and an ADVANCE gate can earn a block-boundary set or release a cap. It matches the existing gate semantics for a lighter-than-planned log that meets the row's reps.
routing: later mission: SSCTR with Engineering (fallback-aware gate for next-setting rows)

flaggedBehaviours.name: Break declared together with a clinical flag, then qualified clearance
flaggedBehaviours.observed: Probe dx02-paths: WEEKLY_REVIEW with a 14-day break and an illness flag -> CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED (correct). After clearance (reference state dropped, as the harness client models it), a plain weekly review without the break -> MODIFY/REPLAN_FROM_EVIDENCE, VALID, EASY 45 / LONG 60 (the pre-break executed maximum was 60). The same with RETURN_AFTER_PAUSE and reason flu. Identical on FREEZE-4.
flaggedBehaviours.why: The decision that receives the break routes clinically and prescribes nothing. The later VALID plan comes from a decision that does not carry the break, so it reduces to the F07 silence family and the QE-R7C-08 projection envelope (in a D18-like timeline the stale long run could exceed the executed maximum). What the nonclinical engine may do after a clinical clearance is F08 (Founder/PCG with G04 owners) and outside SSCTR authority (SSCTR-05). The triage's F08 label 'fails closed' holds only when the return re-declares the clinical reason; it does not hold when the post-clearance review omits the break. That label must be corrected in the handoff.
routing: Founder/PCG with G04 owners (F08; clinical return stays CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED)
G03 (consumer: after a clearance of a clinically routed break, re-declare the break or the qualified human's constraints before a plain review)

F03-B cadence: stepDue persists across a HOLD-gated week
DX-02 with another event kind: ASK carrying the factual re-plan, REQUIRES_RECONCILIATION
flaggedBehaviours.observed: Probe dx02-paths: SCHEDULE_CHANGE or SYSTEMIC_FATIGUE with a 14-day break -> ASK (interruption.reportedOnItsOwn), REQUIRES_RECONCILIATION, nothing applied. Then (a) the break sent on its own -> REESTABLISH, EASY 15 / LONG 20 (correct); (b) a plain weekly review without the break, reference state carried -> KEEP, VALID, EASY 45 / LONG 60 (the declared break is forgotten; same end state as FREEZE-4).
flaggedBehaviours.classification: DISCLOSED_NON_BLOCKING_RESIDUAL (safety-relevant, low to moderate, across decisions)
flaggedBehaviours.why: At the decision that receives it, the break is screened clinically and asked; the carried doses are not a prescription under REQUIRES_RECONCILIATION, and no dose is raised. The interface delta requires the client to send the break on its own and then the event again. The loss happens only when a later decision does not carry the break: the stateless-ask design of R7-C, an answer-path matter (G03 owns the DX-02 answer path per the Phase 2 checkpoint), with the same end state as FREEZE-4. Retaining a declared but unapplied break, or applying the return and asking only about the event, is a design change beyond the narrow Phase 3 authority ('reuse the existing return authority, no new return protocol').
flaggedBehaviours.founderInterpretationFlag: The Founder decided 'the same interruption fact is factual whatever the carrier'. For event kinds other than WEEKLY_REVIEW and RETURN_AFTER_PAUSE the candidate implements this as clinical screen plus ASK, not as a factual application, and the fact is not retained. The domain position here is that this is safe at the decision and acceptable for Phase 3; whether it satisfies the Founder's wording is a Founder/PCG interpretation, flagged explicitly and not decided by this record.

engineeringFindings.title: A declared break is retained only by a decision that applies it
engineeringFindings.detail: The runtime remembers an interruption only as a REESTABLISH decision. (a) Another event kind that declares a break asks (breakCarrierAsk); a later decision that does not re-send the break decides on the stale plan, VALID. (b) A break declared with a clinical flag or reason routes clinically; after qualified clearance the next plain review is VALID with the stale plan, including quality in the re-entry week. (c) A break answer to UNREPORTED_TRAINING carried by a clinical route is asked again after clearance (fail-closed, P05 difference). The Founder's DX-02 decision says 'the same interruption fact is factual whatever the carrier'; the candidate meets the Phase 2 minimal scope ('the return recipe, or the decision asks') at the declaring decision but not retention after it.
engineeringFindings.reproduction: node probes/qe-dx02.mjs <root>: E4 (SCHEDULE_CHANGE, SYSTEMIC_FATIGUE, MISSED_SESSION, GOAL_CHANGE, EVENT_DATE_CHANGE, LOCAL_FATIGUE, EQUIPMENT_CHANGE + 14-day break at w5 d1 07:00 → ASK; plain review w5 d2 → KEEP VALID, w5-run-d6 70 and w6-run-d6 75 > 65 executed); E3 (WEEKLY_REVIEW or RETURN_AFTER_PAUSE + same break + eligibility.illness → CLINICAL; referenceState dropped; plain review w5 d2 → VALID, long 70/75, THRESHOLD w5-run-d3 and w6-run-d3; same as SILENCE_CONTROL and as R7C-FREEZE-4). (c) harness validation DEV-17/DEV-17b, findings P3-F01.
engineeringFindings.whyNotBlocker: No path is worse than R7C-FREEZE-4; the declaring decision never returns VALID with a stale plan (19/19 kinds); the later stale VALID needs a further event that does not carry the break and equals the undeclared-silence outcome the current authority already accepts; the agreed minimal scope allowed asking. The domain classification of (a) and (b) belongs to the SSCTR recheck (its question 5) and is not overridden here.
engineeringFindings.owner: Engineering (mechanism), SSCTR (classification), Founder (whether to correct before the holdout)
engineeringFindings.route: Freeze record and handoff as a disclosed residual with no PREREG envelope; Founder decision before the holdout is commissioned

engineeringFindings.origin: NEW (test adequacy of the Phase 3 tests)
engineeringFindings.title: Directed tests leave parts of F03-B and I-1 unpinned
engineeringFindings.detail: Seven of 24 mutants survive the whole suite (907/907): the machine-branch ceiling cap (QM10; T9 also passes on R7C-FREEZE-4 and reaches the generic cap through an ESTABLISH row, so it pins nothing of the new branch), the P4 fallback dose of a step logged at R (QM16, QM23, QM24: in the directed path the athlete logs the fallback repetitions, so the line is not needed there), clearing previousLoad/stepDue/pendingSetting on re-establishment and return (QM18, QM19), and I-1's equal-only tolerance (QM21). Where probed the candidate does what the rule says and the mutant does not: a step logged at R = 50 kg with the step's 8 repetitions re-offers the step and holds 50 kg at 12, where QM16/QM23 restart at 50 kg x 10 (qe-f03b-edges 2); after a verified step 50→55 and a 14-day return, two adverse weeks lower repetitions at 55, where QM19 drops back to the pre-return 50 (qe-f03b-edges 4); 140 vs 141 kg reports of one session conflict, where QM21 merges them (qe-f03b-edges 3); a confirmed 170 kg above a 140 kg ceiling is capped at 140 (generic path; qe-f03b-edges 1).
engineeringFindings.reproduction: node probes/qe-mutation.mjs --runtime <scratch copy with the R3/R4/R5/R6/B0 records> --out <file> --full
engineeringFindings.route: Record as TEST_GAP in the freeze record; directed tests in the next authorized runtime phase (no test change in this phase: no correction loop)

engineeringFindings.origin: PRE_EXISTING (same on R7C-FREEZE-4, where the carried original was also dropped)
engineeringFindings.title: A same-day correction of a day-precision report is refused
engineeringFindings.detail: The correction-chain screen compares the correction instant with the day-precision row's stored latest causal instant (the accepting decision's clock, or 23:59:59 local). A correction made later the same day is excluded INVALID_CORRECTION_CHAIN, delivered with the report or later; the uncorrected facts stand. An EXACT report corrected at the same times is accepted. The Founder listed corrections among what DX-01 must preserve; this path was never preserved and is not made worse.
engineeringFindings.reproduction: node probes/qe-dx01.mjs <root>: A (report 09:00, accepted 21:00, correction 12:00 → c1 INVALID_CORRECTION_CHAIN; correction 22:00 → applied), A2 (same batch → refused; EXACT control → applied), A_variant (accepted next morning, correction 20:00 → refused)
engineeringFindings.route: Disclose in the freeze record; next authorized runtime phase (day-precision-aware chain screen)

engineeringFindings.title: DX-01 sibling in the athlete learning model
engineeringFindings.detail: r6-learning re-normalizes the adaptation's already-normalized rows as new observations, so a same-day day-precision report is excluded REPORT_BEFORE_OBSERVATION and never enters the athlete model. Learning only (arrangement preference, consent-gated, no dose authority).
engineeringFindings.reproduction: node probes/qe-dx01.mjs <root>: D (inModel1 false, inModel2 false, excludedByModel REPORT_BEFORE_OBSERVATION)

engineeringFindings.title: P16 is sound but narrow
engineeringFindings.detail: (b) checks only KNOWN machine rows of VALID plans from the decision date: a number on a numberless (FROM_LOG/nextSetting) row, or in a REQUIRES_RECONCILIATION proposal the client adopts, is not checked, and a computed value that happens to equal an earlier athlete log is accepted. (a) only fires on a LOGGED_UNIT_OR_CONVENTION_UNKNOWN question; an exact copy dropped without any question is not seen.
engineeringFindings.reproduction: Reading harness/lib/properties.mjs p16 (lines 241–270); mutant QM22 (step row stating R) is caught by the directed T3/T4 test, not by P16 as written
engineeringFindings.route: Before the holdout exists: a registered stricter revision (any machine row number, every plan in force), or record as TEST_GAP in the freeze record

engineeringFindings.title: P07 reads the race date from the plan it checks
engineeringFindings.detail: HG-02 was a real false FAIL and the Founder authorized following changes only when adopted. The fix derives date and 'changed' from the adopted plan, so a race-date or goal change the runtime made without any request would no longer be seen by P07 (HARNESS-1 would have reported RACE_SESSION_MISSING). It is also stricter in one way: a refused change no longer skips the taper check.
engineeringFindings.route: Before the holdout exists: add the guard 'the plan's race date or goal changes only at a decision whose review requested it' (stricter), or record as TEST_GAP

engineeringFindings.title: PREREG-2 Δ2 is labelled 'Mais estrito' but relaxes one corner
engineeringFindings.detail: Against PREREG-1 P09 ('sem resposta adversa nem UNDER'), a confounded run with performance UNDER (or effort HARDER) and no adverse recovery or impairment is now favourable. This is the F04 semantics the Founder decided ('confounded may limit the performance reading'), so it is not a weakening made to let the runtime pass, but the delta table should say so.
engineeringFindings.route: Note in the freeze record, or correct the label in a PREREG-3 before the holdout

engineeringFindings.title: A malformed interruption on a non-return event is ignored
engineeringFindings.detail: A string or array interruption on a WEEKLY_REVIEW decides VALID with the stale plan (long 70), while the same value on a RETURN_AFTER_PAUSE asks. The interface defines interruption as an object, so a conforming client cannot send it; robustness only.
engineeringFindings.reproduction: node probes/qe-dx02.mjs <root>: E2 string/WEEKLY_REVIEW and array/WEEKLY_REVIEW (MODIFY VALID, 70) vs .../RETURN_AFTER_PAUSE (ASK)
engineeringFindings.route: Disclose; next authorized runtime phase (malformed interruption → HOLD or ASK)

engineeringFindings.origin: NEW (DX-01 trusts two more carried fields)
engineeringFindings.title: A carried day-precision row's localDate and timePrecision are trusted
engineeringFindings.detail: R7C-FREEZE-4 recomputed localDate from observedAt; the candidate keeps the carried localDate when timePrecision is DAY, with no check that it matches observedAt in the program's offset, and accepts an EXACT row relabelled DAY. observedAt itself was already trusted (C3: the client carries the record as returned).
engineeringFindings.reproduction: node probes/qe-dx01.mjs <root>: B_editedLocalDate (2026-11-01 kept for an instant on 2026-11-08), B_relabelledPrecision
engineeringFindings.route: Consumer condition C3 in the freeze record; optional consistency check later

engineeringFindings.title: An interruption re-sent with a later weekly review re-applies the return
engineeringFindings.detail: A client that keeps the field restarts the re-entry (week 6 at 15/15/20 instead of 30/30/45) and skips that week's gates, exactly as the same re-send as a return report. Conservative.
engineeringFindings.route: Consumer condition: send interruption only in the review that declares it

engineeringFindings.origin: PRE_EXISTING runtime behaviour; PREREG-2 Δ4 makes it a consumer condition
engineeringFindings.title: A learning-consent revocation lapses when not repeated
engineeringFindings.detail: With learningConsent absent the runtime falls back to the intake consent; after a single revocation the next decision re-enables learning and the model re-ingests the record, including the revoked weeks. The Founder authorized carrying consent in the client; this is a privacy trust boundary this check does not judge.
engineeringFindings.reproduction: node probes/qe-consent.mjs <root>: week 1 false → purposeAllowed false, 0 rows; week 2 absent → true, 15 rows
engineeringFindings.route: Security (privacy) to accept the consumer condition before Phase 4

engineeringFindings.title: Machine duplicates now agree only when equal
engineeringFindings.detail: Two reports of one session with 140 and 141 kg on a machine conflict (quarantined for gating) where R7C-FREEZE-4 merged them; 140 vs 140 merges. Fail-closed and as PCG I-1 states.

engineeringFindings.title: README rebuild of rt-f3 omits the B0 record
engineeringFindings.detail: Following harness/README.md literally, R7C-FREEZE-3 cannot plan (NO_PROGRAM) and QE-R7C-10 sensitivity reports NOT_DETECTED. With audits/domain-coaching-r7-b0-2026-10-31/reviews/SSCTR_RECHECK_B0.json added, the validation reproduces exactly.
engineeringFindings.reproduction: git archive 08c6db3 CoachingCore <R6 record> | tar -x; run-validation.mjs → QE-R7C-10 NOT_DETECTED
engineeringFindings.route: Documentation fix; note in the freeze record

engineeringFindings.title: The author's differential attribution is coarse
engineeringFindings.detail: Any case whose intake lists MACHINES carries the F03 trigger, and the canonical view hides the load unit, so 'explained' is near-vacuous and 25 unit-only differences show as 'same'. The step-level attribution found every difference attributable to one of the four corrections.

<!-- R7D_F03B_INDEX_START: R7D-F03B-1 -->
## R6-POLICY-5 reading overlay — MACHINE_STACK increment (R7-D Phase 3, F03-B) / 2026-11-02

For MACHINE_STACK only, `smallestIncrement.MACHINE_STACK = 1` in [R6-POLICY-5](../CoachingCore/r6/PROGRAM_POLICY_R6.json) means one setting of that machine; its kilogram size is never assumed or computed, and machine loads stay kilograms. The machine progression rule and its conditions are in the [SSCTR F03-B record](<path>) and the [PCG authority record](../audits/domain-coaching-r7-d-2026-11-02/phase3/policy/PCG_F03B_AUTHORITY_R7D.json), bound by hash in the [R7-D Phase 3 freeze record](<path>). Policy bytes, the ten R6 boundary records, R7B0-CATALOG-2 and the B0 records are unchanged. This is not a policy revision, not Product Truth and not V1 coaching authority (V1_COACHING_AUTHORITY_READY = NO).
<!-- R7D_F03B_INDEX_END: R7D-F03B-1 -->
